display.purpose: The bid amount on the lot's detail page, with its unit at 14px and the grid cell it came from on the line below.

headline.purpose: The page title, one per page. The name of the next step on the overview uses the same size with line-height 1.3 and letter-spacing -0.015em.

title.purpose: Card heads, the title of a lot, the title of a log entry.

body.purpose: Running text. The sentence under the next step is held to 72ch.

meta.purpose: The facts line of a log entry or a lot, and the options of a run. Entry times and field labels use the same size at weight 600.

table-head.purpose: Uppercase. Column heads, the term of a fact pair, the label of a counter. Never above a heading.

mono.purpose: The log of a run, model codes, chassis codes, file paths, key caps.

shadows.name: shadow-header
shadows.purpose: Under the sticky header, so that the page passes beneath it.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: The chosen item of a segmented control.

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: The ring around a focused input, with a blue border. A focus mark, not depth.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The curve for movement: a press, a meter, a chevron, the decision row.

motion.name: colour
motion.purpose: Background, border and text colour of buttons, nav items, tiles and inputs.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: A button while it is pressed.

motion.name: meter
motion.purpose: A meter's fill growing to its share. The longest CSS transition.

motion.name: chevron
motion.purpose: The chevron of an opened disclosure.

motion.name: decision-row-enter
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1 and scale 0.97 to 1, 150ms ease-out, origin top right
motion.purpose: The decision row opened with the pointer. Opened with a key it does not animate.

motion.name: log-line-enter
motion.purpose: A new log line. Skipped when more than five lines arrive together.

motion.name: number-tween
motion.value: GSAP, 0.4s, power2.out, snapped to whole numbers
motion.purpose: A counter or a count tile reaching its new value.

motion.name: share-tween
motion.purpose: The meter inside the run console.

motion.name: completion-sweep
motion.purpose: The guide row, once, when a scan ends well. The page reloads after it.

motion.name: now-pulse
motion.value: opacity to 0.35 and back, 1.2s ease-in-out, repeating
motion.purpose: The guide cell being scanned, while the run is running.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The icon of a running run or step.

motion.name: confirm-disarm
motion.purpose: An armed button returns to its first label.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: durations 0.01ms, one iteration, no press movement; scripts write the final value
motion.purpose: Applied when the reader asks for reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
BidBarn's pages are written in the visual language of the Carbarn dashboard, so that the two read as one family when they sit beside each other on the office PC. Jim pinned this on 2026-09-29. The stylesheet is BidBarn's own: one file, `bidbarn.css`, with every token on `:root`. It is light only and declares `color-scheme: light`.

It is a working tool for one person who opens it a session or two a day. The pages are dense enough to hold a day of runs or a queue of lots, and quiet enough that the one thing to do next is easy to find. Text is Manrope at 14px. Surfaces are white cards with a 1px line on a grey-blue ground. The brand blue marks the action that moves the day forward and whatever is live or selected. State is shown as a pill that carries a word.

Motion follows change and nothing else. A page opens still. After that, a number counts to its new value, a meter grows to its share, and the guide row sweeps once when a scan ends. CSS transitions are 120 to 300ms. A reader who asks for reduced motion gets the final values with no movement.
keyCharacteristics: Manrope, one self-hosted variable font (weights 200 to 800), body at 14px and weight 500.
The brand blue for the primary action, the live entry, the selected row and the focus ring.
White cards with a 12px radius and a 1px line, no shadow, on the grey-blue ground.
Pill chips with a tinted ground, a 1px border and ink of the same hue, always with a word.
Uppercase 11px letterspaced labels for table column heads, fact terms and counter labels.
Lucide icons from one sprite, stroke 1.75, 16px by default.
A 72px white sticky header with the Carbarn wordmark, a hairline, the name BidBarn, and the lock pill at the right end.
Tabular numerals wherever numbers are compared or change.
Every font, script and icon is served from the project's own `static/vendor/` folder.

rules.name: The Word With The Colour Rule
rules.body: A status colour never stands alone. Every pill carries its word. A pill that reports a run or a check also carries its Lucide icon. In the guide row the height of a cell changes with its state as well as its colour, and the legend names each state.

rules.name: The Empty Track Exception
rules.body: The guide cells that are not scanned yet are #a3afbf on white, about 2.2:1, below the 3:1 floor for graphics. This is deliberate and it is the only such case. Those cells are the empty track of the row, 4px high. Their meaning is carried elsewhere: the legend names them ("to come", or "not scanned" after the run), the line above the row says "Guide 8 of 46", and the row's accessible label counts them. The value is not a text colour and is not available to any other component.

rules.name: The Data Label Rule
rules.body: The uppercase 11px label names a piece of data: a column, a fact, a counter. It sits directly over its value or its column. It is never placed above a heading or a section title.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Counts, amounts, times and durations use tabular numerals. Numeric table columns are right aligned.

rules.name: The Line Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface is declared once, by its line. Cards, tiles, log entries, tables and notices have a 1px border and no shadow. A shadow belongs to the header and to the chosen segment, nowhere else.

rules.name: The Confirm In Place Rule
rules.body: An action that deserves a second thought is confirmed on the button itself. The first click arms it: the label becomes the confirm words ("Confirm stop", "Confirm approve") and the button turns navy. The second click acts. An armed button disarms after 5 seconds. The button is given the width of its longer label beforehand, so arming moves nothing. No dialog is opened.

rules.name: The Keyboard Is Instant Rule
rules.body: When the decision row is opened with the pointer it fades in and grows from 0.97 over 150ms, from its top right corner. When it is opened with a key it appears at once.

rules.name: The Still On Load Rule
rules.body: Nothing animates when a page opens. What the page opens with is drawn as it is. Only a change that arrives afterwards moves: a counter counts to its new value in 0.4 seconds, a meter grows to its share in 0.3 seconds, a new log line fades in over 150ms unless more than five arrive together. When a scan ends well the cells of the guide row sweep once from 30% to full opacity, 12ms apart. The spinning icon and the pulsing cell mark a run that is running and stop with it.

dos: Do build every page inside the shared shell: the 72px header with the wordmark and the lock pill, the nav, then the page head and its cards.
Do give every state a pill with its word, in the family this document assigns to it.
Do use tabular numerals for counts, amounts, times and durations, and right align numeric columns.
Do show an amount with where it came from: the grid cell under the bid, "grid" or "base" under a changed amount.
Do confirm on the button itself, following the Confirm In Place Rule.
Do keep hover styles behind a fine pointer that can hover, and keep the 2px blue focus ring on every control.
Do use the ease-out curve (`cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)`) for movement, 150ms for colour, 120ms for a press, and 300ms at most for a CSS transition.
Do honour reduced motion: write the final value and move nothing.
Do take icons from the Lucide sprite, at stroke 1.75.
Do use the tokens on `:root`. Where the stylesheet writes a value straight into a rule, treat it as that component's own value.
donts: Don't add a dark theme or a `prefers-color-scheme` branch. The pages are light only, like the Carbarn dashboard.
Don't place the uppercase 11px label above a heading or a section title. It names data.
Don't use the grey of the cells to come (#a3afbf) anywhere else, and don't use `ink-faint` for text.
Don't put a shadow on a card, a tile, a log entry or a notice.
Don't animate anything when a page opens, and don't animate what a key opens.
Don't open a dialog to confirm an action.
Don't show a state by colour alone.
Don't use a Unicode mark or an emoji where an icon belongs.
Don't load a font, a script or an icon from the network. Everything is served from `static/vendor/`.
Don't introduce a second typeface for headings. Manrope carries every level.
